Peak and late sampling windows were deliberately chosen to contrast scarce versus high pollinator activity. Legitimate oil-bee visit marks occurred on 7.5% of peak flowers (134) versus 93.6% of late flowers (140). The binomial seed-set model reports flowering-time estimate +1.55 (SE 0.25), treatment +1.41 (SE 0.24), and interaction -1.26 (SE 0.31); together with the reported group pattern these signs identify +1.55 as the late-versus-peak natural-pollination log-odds contrast. Variance=0.25^2. Model n=173 plants across flowering-time × pollination-treatment groups. Dataset is available upon request.

Strict contrast restricted to 2007 because bumble-bee activity was measured contemporaneously only that year. Early/mid-July had very low visits by queens; worker bees appeared in late July and visit frequency increased abruptly and stayed high through August. Table 4 intact natural seed set: HIS M high-overlap mean=0.77 SE=0.03 n=24 versus E low-overlap mean=0.62 SE=0.04 n=24. Source values are mean±SE; SD=SE*sqrt(n), then Hedges g for M minus E gives g=0.8518282660, variance=0.0885105687.

2015 flowering onset was manipulated into four weekly cohorts (n=10 each). Pollinator visitation was measured contemporaneously and declined >5-fold from week 1 to week 4, fixing week 1 as the higher-availability window before using seed-set values. Dissertation Table 2.2 reports relative observed seed-set means [0.85,1.00,0.91,0.69]; the same four-group outcome has F(3,36)=1.01. For the balanced design, F(3,36)=MS_between/MS_within deterministically recovers pooled within-group variance on the same relative scale. The residual standardizer has df=36, so the Hedges correction and denominator-uncertainty term use df=36. Hedges g for high-overlap week 1 minus low-overlap week 4 is +0.3815303645, variance=0.1937181574. The common relative scaling cancels in the SMD; no missing variance or slope conversion is used.
